statements.markdown:
**Proof.** Fix $t<T<T'<1$ and a shrinking interval
$[t-\delta_n,t+\delta_n)\subset(0,T)$. Approximate $\gamma$ by
$$
h_n=\max\{\epsilon_n,\min\{K_n,
                  \eta_n\lfloor\gamma/\eta_n\rfloor\}\},
$$
where $0<\epsilon_n<c<K_n$, $\epsilon_n,\eta_n\downarrow0$ and
$K_n\uparrow\infty$. Use $\min(c,h_n)$ to the left of the interval,
$c$ on it, and $\max(c,h_n)$ to its right. Monotonicity makes these
positive, nondecreasing, right-continuous finite-step coefficients
$\gamma_n$. Clipping toward $c$ outside the interval cannot increase
the error, and
$$
\|\gamma_n-\gamma\|_1
\le\epsilon_n+\eta_n+\int_0^1(\gamma-K_n)_+\,ds
 +2\delta_n\sup_{|s-t|\le\delta_n}|\gamma(s)-c|
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{4.3}
$$
Integrability controls the capped tail and continuity at $t$ the last
term. Choose smooth terminal parameters $M_n\ge\max(n,K_n)$.
The terminal values then converge uniformly to $|x|$, and the coefficient
masses have a common bound. The finite-step inequality of §4.4 applies
at $t$, where every $\gamma_n$ equals the same positive $c$.
statements.note: Lean builds no plateau at t: it samples at grid times tending to t, and the height tends to c by continuity.
statements.section: 4.5 Coercivity at a fixed time and on plateaus

To obtain Lemma 2 for an integrable coefficient, choose positive
monotone step coefficients $\gamma_n$ that keep the plateau near a
fixed interior time, with $\|\gamma_n-\gamma\|_1\to0$, and terminal
parameters $M_n\geq\|\gamma_n\|_\infty$ with $M_n\to\infty$.

fixed strip below one, and the diffusions driven by the same Brownian
motion converge
(see [OpenAI (2026a), Lemmas 2.1–2.2 and Proposition 5.1][FS]). Only
$v,w,z$ remain in (5), so the auxiliary logarithmic derivative $s$
needs no convergence theorem.

On a fixed strip containing $t$ and ending before one, compact-strip
regularity gives uniform spatial convergence and bounds through order
four. The next derivative bounds give a common spatial Lipschitz
constant for those derivatives. Coupling with the same Brownian motion
and applying Gronwall gives a deterministic bound
$\sup_{s\le T}|X_s^n-X_s|\to0$. If $D_k^n=\partial_x^k\Phi_n$
and $D_k=\partial_x^k\Phi$, then, for $1\le k\le4$,

$$
|D_k^n(t,X_t^n)-D_k(t,X_t)|
\le\|D_k^n-D_k\|_{\infty,[0,T]\times\mathbb R}
   +C_{k,T}|X_t^n-X_t|\longrightarrow0.
$$

statements.markdown:
To make this quantitative, let $V,W,Z$ bound both the limiting and approximating
$v,w,z$, and let $e_v,e_w,e_z$ bound their coupled evaluation errors.
Uniform spatial convergence and the path bound above give these errors
with $e_v,e_w,e_z\to0$. Difference-of-powers identities give
$$
\begin{aligned}
|\mathbb E\mathcal C(v_n,w_n,z_n)-\mathbb E\mathcal C(v,w,z)|
 &\le(12W^2+24V^3)e_v+24VW e_w+2Ze_z,\\
|\mathbb E v_n^4-\mathbb E v^4|&\le4V^3e_v,
\end{aligned}
$$
where $\mathcal C(v,w,z)=z^2-12vw^2+6v^4$. These constants depend only
on the common strip and the coefficient mass bound, and in particular are
independent of the plateau width.
statements.note: Not in the Lean: it has no difference-of-powers bounds. Both limits pass by dominated convergence, so these constants do not appear.
